references.text: Jacob sets up a stone pillar again, this time in Bethel, and pours oil over it, just as he did before.
God reminds Jacob of the stone at Bethel that he anointed and commands him to return to the land of Canaan.
Jacob sets up a stone pillar as a witness to the covenant between him and Laban.
Joshua takes a large stone and sets it up under the oak tree near the Lord's sanctuary as a witness, paralleling Jacob's practice of setting up stone pillars.
Moses sets up twelve stone pillars at the foot of Mount Sinai, paralleling the practice of erecting stone monuments as memorials.
Samuel sets up a stone and calls it Ebenezer as a memorial, paralleling Jacob's stone pillar at Bethel.
This is the immediate background to the event in the source verse; the same stone is first used as a pillow and later as a sacred memorial pillar.
Thematic parallel: Isaac's altar building confirms that Jacob's raising of a stone pillar is part of the same tradition for marking God's revelations.
